assessments.reasoning: The specification explicitly includes function and method calls in the ordering rule for operands of all three named constructs. Ordering applies to calls reached during evaluation, with argument evaluation preceding invocation of the enclosing call.

challenge.method: Compare sibling calls, a call nested in an argument, a short-circuited call, and an ordinary variable read.
challenge.results: Reached sibling calls follow source order. The nested call supplies its value before the enclosing invocation. Short-circuiting can omit a call entirely, and the passage leaves some reads unordered relative to calls.

limitations: This does not fix every operand's relative evaluation order or require evaluation of a call suppressed by short-circuiting.
The direction applies to function-local evaluation and preserves call-argument dependencies. Some other operand evaluations have unspecified relative order, and short-circuiting can suppress calls.
